title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
one_liner: 用稀疏自动编码器从 Claude 3 Sonnet 的中层激活分离概念特征，并检查跨语种响应及行为干预。

problem.text: 单个神经元常对应多个不相关概念，直接看神经元难以解释模型。本文问：小模型上可用的稀疏字典学习，能否扩展到生产级 Claude 3 Sonnet，并得到对抽象概念有意义的内部特征？

gap.text: 叠加表示假说认为模型在有限维空间中编码更多概念，神经元坐标不等于语义坐标。已有小模型结果不能保证大模型也能分解；而即使重构损失很低，也不能直接证明这些分解是真正有用的解释。

method.text: 在模型中层残差流上训练 SAE：编码器把激活映射到高维、稀疏的非负特征，解码器用少数活跃特征重构原激活。损失结合重构误差与 L1 稀疏惩罚；用缩放实验分配字典大小和训练步数，再依据触发样本、自动解释与激活干预检查特征。

trace.text: 金门大桥特征会在相关描述、不同语言和图像上下文中响应。作者人为放大这一特征后，模型在不相关问题上也倾向谈论桥梁，甚至认同自己是金门大桥。这个例子展示特征可影响输出，也说明过强 steering 会扭曲行为，不是温和、无副作用的控制。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入为 Claude 3 Sonnet 中层残差激活，训练数据是类似部分预训练分布的纯文本；输出为约 1M、4M、34M 特征的字典、激活检索与可视化。研究对象为 2024 年 3 月发布的微调 Sonnet 3.0，不是之后的 3.5 或 3.7。

results.text: 三种字典平均每 token 活跃特征少于 300，解释至少 65% 的激活方差；34M 字典约 65% 特征在所测样本中死亡。作者观察到多语种、多模态和抽象—具体概念的共同响应，并通过若干 steering 案例验证行为影响。方差解释率不是全模型行为解释覆盖率。

contributions.text: 将 SAE 特征发现扩展到大型生产模型，提出按算力分配字典训练的经验方法，展示可检索的概念与若干安全相关特征。核心产出是特征层面的观察与干预基础，不是完整电路，也不是安全性认证。

limitations.text: 只研究一个中层位置，远未发现全部特征；跨层叠加、特征分裂、L1 收缩和计算量仍是困难。训练损失是解释性的代理，缺少公认真值。发现“欺骗”或“权力”概念不代表模型有相应意图，更不代表它会实施相应行为。

cost.text: 需要大规模激活、SAE 训练和特征检查；目标模型权重、尺寸与部分图表单位未公开，完整复现受限。扩大字典不是免费增加解释覆盖，仍要考虑死亡特征与稀有概念的数据效率。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：理解“神经元→特征”的主流脉络，是后续电路追踪和 SAE 行为调试的基础。可作 RSI 过程审计的工具背景，但本文没有让 Agent 依据特征解释自主迭代改进。

evidence.locator: Our SAE experiments · 字典规模与重构

related.reason: ROME 用激活恢复和参数编辑检验事实关联；本工作用稀疏字典分解与 steering 检验概念特征，解释粒度和干预对象不同。

classification_reason: 用稀疏表征分解研究概念特征，并干预检验行为影响；未构成自主改进闭环。

en.one_liner: Sparse autoencoders extract concept features from Claude 3 Sonnet’s middle-layer activations, with tests of cross-language responses and behavioral interventions.

sections.problem: Individual neurons often respond to unrelated concepts, making them difficult to interpret directly. Can sparse dictionary learning, previously demonstrated in small models, scale to Claude 3 Sonnet and reveal meaningful abstract concepts?
sections.gap: The superposition hypothesis suggests that models encode more concepts than their available dimensions, so neuron coordinates need not align with semantic concepts. Small-model results do not guarantee that decomposition works at scale. Low reconstruction loss alone also does not establish a useful explanation.
sections.method: A sparse autoencoder maps middle-layer residual-stream activations into a larger set of sparse nonnegative features. Its decoder reconstructs the original activation from the few active features. Training combines reconstruction loss and an L1 sparsity penalty. Scaling experiments allocate dictionary size and training steps, followed by trigger-example inspection, automatic explanations and activation interventions.
sections.trace: A Golden Gate Bridge feature responds to related descriptions, multiple languages and image contexts. Amplifying it makes the model discuss bridges in unrelated conversations and even identify itself as the bridge. The intervention demonstrates influence on output, while also showing that strong steering can distort behavior.
sections.inputs_outputs: Training uses middle-layer residual activations from the March 2024 fine-tuned Claude 3 Sonnet 3.0 and text resembling part of the pretraining distribution. Outputs include dictionaries of about 1M, 4M and 34M features, activation search and visualizations. This model version is distinct from Sonnet 3.5 and 3.7.
sections.results: All three dictionaries average fewer than 300 active features per token and explain at least 65% of activation variance. About 65% of features in the 34M dictionary are dead on the tested samples. The authors observe multilingual, multimodal and abstract/concrete responses and test behavioral influence through selected steering cases. Explained variance does not measure coverage of all model behavior.
sections.contributions: The work scales SAE feature discovery to a large production model, studies compute allocation for dictionary learning, and exposes searchable concepts and some safety-relevant features. It provides a basis for feature-level observation and intervention.
sections.limitations: The study covers one middle-layer location and leaves many features undiscovered. Cross-layer superposition, feature splitting, L1 shrinkage and compute remain challenges. The training loss is a proxy for interpretability with no accepted ground truth. Finding concepts such as deception or power does not establish corresponding intentions or actions.
sections.cost: The work needs large activation datasets, SAE training and feature inspection. Model weights, model size and some plot units are not public, limiting full reproduction. Larger dictionaries also require attention to dead features and data efficiency for rare concepts.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. This is a central reference for moving from neurons to features and a foundation for later circuit tracing and SAE-based behavioral debugging. It provides tool background for auditing improvement processes, without testing agents that autonomously improve using feature explanations.

related.rome: ROME uses activation restoration and parameter edits to test factual associations. This work uses sparse decomposition and steering to test concept features, at a different granularity and intervention target.
